## Review — concurrency/stability fixes in uncommitted working tree (vs 8159042)

### Findings (ranked)

**1. MAJOR | Source/Communication.Shared/Framing/LengthPrefixFrameReader.cs:Dispose (`_buffer` Return) + MessagePipeline.cs:146**
Dispose returns the accumulation buffer to `ArrayPool.Shared` while the receive loop may still be mid-`ReadAsync` into it. Evidence: `MessagePipeline.Dispose` does `cts.Cancel()` (does not synchronously abort an in-flight socket read), then `_frameReader?.Dispose()`; the channel/socket is only closed afterwards by `Session.MarkDisconnected` (pipeline.Dispose → channel.Dispose). `ReadFrameAsync` reads directly into `_buffer.AsMemory(_end)` (StreamByteChannel → `stream.ReadAsync(buffer)`), so the pinned array is still a live read target when returned to the pool. Another renter (same process, e.g. another session's `PooledBufferWriter` using the same pool) can then write the same array concurrently → silent cross-component data corruption on every disconnect where the receive loop is blocked in read (its steady state). Fix: only `Return` when no read is in flight (Interlocked flag set around `channel.ReadAsync`, Dispose checks it), otherwise leave the one buffer to GC — or drop the `Return` from Dispose entirely.

**2. MINOR | Source/Communication.Shared/Messages/MessagePipeline.cs:161,176,184 (EnqueueAsync)**
Dispose race can surface `ObjectDisposedException` instead of `InvalidOperationException`: `_sendSlots.WaitAsync(_cts.Token)` with semaphore/CTS already disposed (`_cts.Token` accessor throws ODE after `_cts.Dispose()`), and `_sendSlots.Release()` in the post-WaitAsync stopped check. Contract F2-6 (faulted Task, no sync throw) still holds — EnqueueAsync is async so all paths yield a faulted Task — but the exception type is inconsistent at shutdown. Fix: catch `ObjectDisposedException` in EnqueueAsync and translate to `InvalidOperationException`.
